data.summary: The 10‑week plan introduces each AP Calculus AB unit in a logical order, allocating 5 study hours per week. Early weeks focus on foundational limits and differentiation, then move through applications, integration, and differential equations. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to solidify understanding and improve exam speed.

weeks.focus: Foundations: limits and basic differentiation concepts
tasks: Watch the live class on limits (11000) and take detailed notes on 1.1 and 1.2.
Do 8 practice problems estimating limits from graphs (1.1) and tables (1.2).
Watch the live class on average/instantaneous rates (11001) and complete the guided worksheet.
Complete 10 derivative‑definition problems (2.1) and check answers with the scoring guide.
Review class notes on power rule (2.5) and solve 12 mixed‑rule derivative problems.
Practice estimating derivatives at points (2.3) with 6 graph‑based questions.
Read the textbook section on continuity ↔ differentiability (2.4) and write a one‑page summary.
Attend live class on Mean Value Theorem (11004) and complete the in‑class worksheet.
Watch the recorded tutorial on the chain rule and do 10 chain‑rule derivative problems.
Do 8 implicit differentiation problems (including related rates set‑ups) and verify each step.
Create a cheat sheet listing chain‑rule and implicit‑diff formulas.
Solve 6 problems differentiating inverse functions (3.3).
Complete 8 derivative problems involving inverse trig functions (3.4).
Check answers against the AP scoring guidelines and note common errors.
Do 5 motion‑context problems connecting position, velocity, acceleration (4.2).
Complete 6 related‑rates problems (4.4) and write a brief explanation of each set‑up.
Answer 4 rate‑of‑change in non‑motion contexts (4.3).
Summarize how derivative meaning changes with context (4.1) in a paragraph.
Identify critical points and classify them in 8 functions (5.2).
Determine increasing/decreasing intervals for 6 functions (5.3).
Apply the First Derivative Test to 5 functions and record conclusions (5.4).
Review the Mean Value Theorem notes from week 2.
Read the section on accumulation of change (6.1) and write 3 real‑world examples.
Complete 10 Riemann‑sum approximation problems (6.2 & 6.3) using left, right, and midpoint sums.
Translate a summation notation problem into a definite integral (6.3).

weeks.focus: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and applications
tasks: Solve 8 problems applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (6.4).
Find average values of functions on given intervals (8.1) in 6 calculations.
Work through 5 position‑velocity‑acceleration integration problems (8.2).
Model 4 real‑world situations with differential equations (7.1).
Sketch slope fields for 3 differential equations (7.3).
Practice reasoning from slope fields by answering 5 interpretation questions (7.4).
Take a 55‑minute full‑length AP practice section covering all units; mark answers against the scoring guide.
Review every missed question, rewriting the solution step‑by‑step.
Do a rapid‑fire set of 20 mixed‑topic free‑response questions (2 per unit) in 30 minutes.
Create a final one‑page cheat sheet summarizing key formulas and strategies.

data.final_week_advice: On the day before the exam, skim your cheat sheet, do a short 15‑minute warm‑up of a few FRQs, and focus on breathing and confidence. Trust the systematic practice you’ve built over the past weeks.
